From: Priya Malhotra <security@aurum.ai>

Cc: L. Patel <patel.legal@aurum.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data localization carveouts + erase certification questions

Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick onboarding so far. As we complete our DPA review there are two items our security and legal teams flagged that we need explicit language for before we can sign:

1) Geo-carveouts for backups: we require that any scheduled backups that include EU customer data either be kept onshore (EU) or be explicitly excluded from cross-border backup flows unless a written exception is approved. We understand you offer onshore snapshots for Dedicated customers — need confirmation of wording and how exceptions are requested/approved.

2) Erase certification cadence and scope: we need an attestation that erasure requests will be completed within the agreed erase window (30 days for primary + 90 days for backup restore retention), and that Redwood can provide a certification report (signed) within 10 business days of request.

Can you send proposed redline language and examples of the certification deliverable? Also attaching a short checklist of evidence items we typically accept (SOCs, wipe runbook snippets, screenshots).

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Malhotra
Head of Security, Aurum AI
security@aurum.ai

Subject: Re: Data localization carveouts + erase certification questions

Priya —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've attached a proposed redline that addresses both items and a short playbook excerpt showing the erase certification format. High-level responses below, and then proposed contract language excerpts in the attached docx: 

- Geo-carveouts for backups: we can add a carveout table in the DPA where customers can select: (a) mirror backups onshore, (b) exclude backups from cross-border transfer, or (c) allow cross-border with documented exception. Exceptions are approved via a signed change order routed through our Security & Contracts team; turnaround target is 5 business days for routine requests.

- Erase certification: we can confirm a signed attestation within 10 business days after the final erasure run is completed. For backups, our standard policy is a 90-day retention for cold snapshots before physical rotation; we will include a clause allowing customers to require accelerated backup wipe if they select the ‘onshore mirror’ option. Certification will include: wipe run ID, affected namespaces, timestamp window, and verification hash where applicable.

Next steps: Attached redline (redwood_proposed_dpa_redline.docx) includes two alternative paragraphs for the backup carveout. Karthik, can you review the alternate (A/B) wording I flagged? Olga — please pull the most recent erase runbook snippet for the attached playbook.

If that looks acceptable to Aurum, happy to schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the redline and lock the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Geo carveouts + erase certification — internal suggested edits

Forwarding internal suggested language — see flagged changes in the attached doc (I added a short exceptions process and tightened the backup acceleration trigger). Key points I recommend we propose to Aurum as our standard compromise: 

- Keep the carveout selector (mirror / exclude / exception). For the exception path, require a documented business justification and an exception approval ticket; exception limited to 12 months then reviewed.
- For backup wipe: propose a 60-day default for accelerated backup wipe when customer elects onshore mirror, unless otherwise negotiated. This avoids operational burden of immediate 30-day backup flush.
- Certification: we suggest the attestation includes a statement of method (logical deletion vs. physical overwrite) and whether any backups were restored within the erase window (so the customer can reconcile). We can provide hashes for object-level stores; for certain encrypted snapshots we will provide wipe logs and confirmation of key destruction where applicable.

Olga — please confirm the feasibility of 60-day accelerated wipe and sample header structure for attestations; I'll fold into the redline and send back to Aurum.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Geo carveouts and erase certification playbook — counters

Evelyn / Karthik —

Thanks for the suggested wording and the two alternatives. A few counterpoints from our legal/security side: 

1) Exception duration: 12 months is acceptable if there is an automatic renewal only with explicit re-authorization by Aurum; please update the exception language to require reauthorization, and include a notification obligation 30 days before expiry.

2) Accelerated backup wipe window: we need a maximum of 45 days (not 60) from request to canary wipe completion for onshore mirrors. If operationally infeasible provide escalation path and milestone reporting at 15-day intervals.

3) Certification content: the attestation should include a signatory from Redwood’s security operations team (name + title), and a single line confirming whether backup snapshots were recreated/restored during the erase window. We can accept the proposed verification hashes or key destruction confirmation.

If you can accept these three items I'll get Aurum's GC to review and aim to move to signature. Please send an updated redline reflecting these points.

Regards,
L. Patel
Counsel, Aurum AI
patel.legal@aurum.ai
